answer_text:
Let

\[
T=\int_{0}^{\ln 2} \frac{2 e^{3x}+e^{2x}-1}{e^{3x}+e^{2x}-e^{x}+1}\,dx.
\]

Set

\[
u=e^x,\qquad dx=\frac{du}{u}.
\]

When \(x=0\), \(u=1\); when \(x=\ln 2\), \(u=2\). Then

\[
T=\int_1^2 \frac{2u^3+u^2-1}{u^3+u^2-u+1}\cdot \frac{du}{u}.
\]

Let

\[
P(u)=u^3+u^2-u+1.
\]

Then

\[
P'(u)=3u^2+2u-1.
\]

Now observe that

\[
uP'(u)-P(u)
=u(3u^2+2u-1)-(u^3+u^2-u+1)
=2u^3+u^2-1.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\frac{2u^3+u^2-1}{uP(u)}
=\frac{P'(u)}{P(u)}-\frac{1}{u}.
\]

So

\[
T=\int_1^2 \left(\frac{P'(u)}{P(u)}-\frac{1}{u}\right)du.
\]

Hence

\[
T=\left[\ln P(u)-\ln u\right]_1^2.
\]

Compute:

\[
P(2)=8+4-2+1=11,
\]
\[
P(1)=1+1-1+1=2.
\]

Thus

\[
T=(\ln 11-\ln 2)-(\ln 2-\ln 1)
=\ln 11-2\ln 2
=\ln\left(\frac{11}{4}\right).
\]

Therefore,

\[
e^T=\frac{11}{4}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{11}{4}}
\]
